title.title: Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem
title.subtitle: Claim: every invertible mixing transformation of any probability space is mixing of every order

beats.text: Mixing: events far apart in time become independent
Rokhlin, 1949: does that force three or more events to decouple jointly?

plain: Stir cream into coffee: two far-apart moments look independent. Does that make three moments independent too?

steps: Suppose some order of mixing fails, and take the smallest one
Boil it down to a simple process whose smaller groups already decouple
Show such a process must decouple fully: a contradiction

voice.text: Mixing makes two distant events independent. Rokhlin asked whether three or more must follow.
Take the smallest failing order, simplify it, and show it cannot fail at all.
